issues.description: SQL injection vulnerability in searchTodos() - Direct string interpolation of user input into SQL query using template literals
issues.suggestion: Use parameterized queries: const query = 'SELECT * FROM todos WHERE title LIKE ? OR description LIKE ?'; const pattern = `%${keyword}%`; await db.query(query, [pattern, pattern]);

issues.description: SQL injection vulnerability in searchTodosByStatus() - Direct string concatenation of user input without validation or parameterization
issues.suggestion: Use parameterized query and change parameter type to boolean: const query = 'SELECT * FROM todos WHERE completed = ?'; await db.query(query, [completed]);

issues.description: SQL injection vulnerability in getTodosByUser() - Template literal with userId directly embedded in JOIN query
issues.suggestion: Use parameterized query: const query = 'SELECT t.* FROM todos t JOIN user_todos ut ON t.id = ut.todo_id WHERE ut.user_id = ?'; await db.query(query, [userId]);

issues.description: Incorrect parameter type - searchTodosByStatus accepts string but completed field should be boolean
issues.suggestion: Change function signature to: export async function searchTodosByStatus(completed: boolean): Promise<Todo[]>

issues.description: Missing input validation in searchTodos() - No checks for empty, null, or excessively long keywords
issues.suggestion: Add validation: if (!keyword || keyword.trim().length === 0) { throw new Error('Keyword required'); } if (keyword.length > 100) { throw new Error('Keyword too long'); }

issues.description: Missing input validation in getTodosByUser() - No UUID format validation or empty string check
issues.suggestion: Add validation: if (!userId || userId.trim().length === 0) { throw new Error('User ID required'); } const uuidPattern = /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/i; if (!uuidPattern.test(userId)) { throw new Error('Invalid UUID'); }

issues.description: No error handling - Database errors will propagate unhandled
issues.suggestion: Wrap database operations in try-catch: try { /* query */ } catch (error) { throw new Error(`Failed to search todos: ${error.message}`); }

issues.description: Using SELECT * over-fetches data and LIKE with leading wildcard prevents index usage
issues.suggestion: Use specific columns and add LIMIT: SELECT id, title, description, completed, created_at FROM todos WHERE title LIKE ? OR description LIKE ? LIMIT 50

issues.description: Unsafe type casting with 'as Todo[]' without runtime validation
issues.suggestion: Add runtime validation with Zod or similar: const TodoArraySchema = z.array(TodoSchema); return TodoArraySchema.parse(rows);

issues.description: Inconsistent SQL query formatting - Uses string concatenation instead of template literals
issues.suggestion: Use consistent multi-line template literals for all SQL queries

codeQuality.summary: This file contains 3 critical SQL injection vulnerabilities in all newly added functions. The code uses direct string concatenation/interpolation to build SQL queries without parameterization, making it extremely vulnerable to SQL injection attacks. Additional issues include missing input validation, no error handling, incorrect type usage (string instead of boolean), and unsafe type casting. The code quality score is severely impacted by these critical security flaws.

suggestions.description: Replace SQL string interpolation with parameterized queries to prevent SQL injection
suggestions.before:
const query = `SELECT * FROM todos WHERE title LIKE '%${keyword}%' OR description LIKE '%${keyword}%'`;
const rows = await db.query(query);
suggestions.benefits: Prevents SQL injection attacks, follows database security best practices, allows database to optimize query plan

suggestions.description: Replace string concatenation with parameterized query and fix parameter type
suggestions.benefits: Fixes critical SQL injection vulnerability, improves type safety with boolean parameter, prevents invalid input values

suggestions.description: Replace template literal SQL injection with parameterized query
suggestions.before:
const query = `SELECT t.* FROM todos t JOIN user_todos ut ON t.id = ut.todo_id WHERE ut.user_id = '${userId}'`;
const rows = await db.query(query);
suggestions.after:
const query = `SELECT t.* FROM todos t JOIN user_todos ut ON t.id = ut.todo_id WHERE ut.user_id = ?`;
const rows = await db.query(query, [userId]);
suggestions.benefits: Prevents SQL injection in JOIN queries, protects against unauthorized access to other users' data

refactorings.summary: Multiple critical refactorings needed to address security vulnerabilities and improve code quality. Primary focus should be replacing all string concatenation with parameterized queries, adding input validation, and improving type safety. Additional improvements include extracting validation helpers, adding error handling, and optimizing query performance.

recommendations.description: Replace all SQL string concatenation/interpolation with parameterized queries immediately. All three functions (searchTodos, searchTodosByStatus, getTodosByUser) are vulnerable to SQL injection attacks.
Add comprehensive security tests to verify SQL injection protection. Test with malicious inputs like "'; DROP TABLE todos; --" and "' OR '1'='1" to ensure parameterized queries work correctly.
Change searchTodosByStatus parameter type from string to boolean. The current implementation accepts any string value, which is type-unsafe and error-prone.
Add input validation to all functions. Validate that keywords are not empty, user IDs match expected format (UUID), and implement length limits to prevent DoS attacks.
Implement unit tests covering all edge cases: empty inputs, null values, special characters, non-existent users, and database errors. Target minimum 80% code coverage.
Add try-catch blocks to handle database errors gracefully. Provide meaningful error messages for debugging and better user experience.
Optimize queries by selecting specific columns instead of SELECT *, add LIMIT clauses to prevent large result sets, and consider full-text search indexes for better performance.
Extract validation logic into reusable helper functions and standardize SQL query formatting for consistency and maintainability.
